correctness.rationale: A cyclic width-w maximum is continuous piecewise affine in input, with strict-order slopes given by site selectors. For selector counts c_j, exact Gini coarea makes the norm the maximum t(n-t)/[k(n-k)] on cuts S, with t=sum_{j in S} c_j. For 2w<=n, each c_j<=w, and the cases kw<=n/2 and kw>n/2 yield the stated upper w(n-w)/(n-1) by the occupancy and quadratic bounds. For 2w>=n the unique global peak wins all w windows containing it, forcing any output cut count t either <=n-w or >=w. This gives numerator at most w(n-w), denominator at least n-1. A small perturbation of one unique global maximum changes exactly w output coordinates, giving sharp equality. The n=2/w=n degenerate cases were checked. Fresh exhaustive strict-order selection and all-cut rational tests for all n=2..6, all 1<=w<=n matched the formula. Finite cases are corroboration only.
